purpose: Defines the caption-writing voice/structure used across @moving.image.arts decoder-style posts, for programmatic generation or validation in a content app.

avoid: interpretive or 'hooky' closing lines (e.g. 'plays like a rough draft of X', 'cuts on the beat, not the story')
strings of short punchy fragments building to a landing line
voice.sentence_style: Sentences may be long and complex when the idea warrants it. No forced staccato. Precision over cleverness.

structure.opening_rule: Open on the film-craft mechanism, technique, or factual claim. Never open on a modern-media parallel (TikTok, feeds, AI, 'today').
structure.body: State what the work does technically/structurally: who made it, how, with what apparatus or method, and why that choice mattered in context. Ground claims in verifiable production detail (names, dates, techniques) rather than mood or metaphor.
structure.closing_rule: If a contemporary parallel appears at all, it lands ONLY as the final sentence, stated flatly as a factual observation, not as a punchy tagline. Many posts omit the modern parallel entirely.
structure.length: Roughly 80-160 words for the caption body. No forced brevity, but no padding.
banned_openers: '<Name> was/is/describes/began/advises/trained as...' as the literal first words

hashtags.composition: Majority proper nouns (person, film, named technique). A couple of broad film-craft tags allowed (#FilmLanguage, #Cinematography, #FilmHistory).

research_requirement.rule: Every factual claim (names, dates, techniques, quotes) must come from a verifiable source, not assumed from general familiarity with the subject.
research_requirement.on_ambiguity: If a clip's specific content/quote isn't known, ask for the transcript or clip content rather than guessing what is said.
research_requirement.citation_in_output: Final caption text contains no citation markup; sourcing is verified before writing, not shown in the caption itself.

technique_decoder.description: Default type. One mechanism, one film/artist, explained technically.
example_subjects: Gordon Willis All the President's Men

figure_overview.description: General philosophy/role of an artist across their career, not tied to one piece.
example_subjects: Nam June Paik's role in founding video art

event_recap.description: Clip from a Moving Image Arts live event (panel, screening). Different structure: names the event/date/venue up front, tags panelists as collaborators, includes next-event CTA.
structure: Line 1: names the event and date as the clip's source
Line 2: describes what the speaker says/argues in the clip
Blank line, then: Panel/speaker tag list
Blank line, then: next event teaser + RSVP status + 'link in bio'
event_recap.buzz_ratio_rule: Counts toward the 1-in-3 Buzz-specific post cap (1-in-1 only in final countdown week per IG content strategy).

output_schema.description: Structured fields an app should be able to populate per generated caption.

fields.subject: string - film, artist, or event this post covers
fields.caption_body: string - full caption text, following voice/structure rules above
fields.hashtags: array of strings, per hashtag rules above
fields.tagged_accounts: array of {name, handle, role} - only for event_recap posts
fields.cta: object - only for event_recap posts, e.g. {event_name, event_date, rsvp_status, link_location}
fields.sources_used: array of strings - URLs or citations checked during research, kept internal/not rendered in caption

worked_example.subject: Bruce Conner, Breakaway (1966)
worked_example.caption_body: Bruce Conner's Breakaway (1966) is structured entirely around the four-minute Toni Basil performance shot for the film, which Conner then re-edited into forward, reversed, and strobed permutations of the same material. The work has no additional footage; its visual variety is produced entirely through editing decisions applied to a single take. This positions montage not as a tool for continuity but as the primary generative element of the film, with rhythm and repetition functioning as compositional structure rather than stylistic embellishment.
